results.problem: Weak villainy of repeated disjoint unions (mG)
results.bound: 0 \le mF_k(G) - \beta_k(mG) \le r\big(F_k(G) - \beta_k(G)\big) \text{ where } m = qk + r, 0 \le r < k; \text{ in particular } \beta_k(mG) = mF_k(G) \text{ when } k \mid m, \text{ and } \lim_{m\to\infty} \beta_k(mG)/m = F_k(G)
results.quote: Then \(0\le mF_k(G)-\beta_k(mG)\le r\big(F_k(G)-\beta_k(G)\big)\). In particular, \(\beta_k(mG)=mF_k(G)\) whenever \(k|m\), and \(\lim_{m\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\beta_k(mG)}{m}=F_k(G)\).

results.problem: Weak villainy stabilization for repeated disjoint unions
results.bound: For m \ge N = (k-1)M with M = (2(k-1)n+1)^{k-1}, the defect mF_k(G) - \beta_k(mG) is eventually periodic with least period h = \gcd\{\ell \ge 1 : \beta_k(\ell G) = \ell F_k(G)\}, h \mid k, computable using \ell \le M; \beta_k(mG) = mF \iff h \mid m for m \ge N
results.quote: The number h is the least eventual period of the defect sequence d_m=mF-\beta_k(mG): it is the least positive integer for which d_{m+h}=d_m for all sufficiently large m. In particular, for m\ge N, \beta_k(mG)=mF \Longleftrightarrow h|m. Moreover, h=\gcd\{1\le\ell\le M:\beta_k(\ell G)=\ell F\}.

results.problem: Ordinary villainy asymptotic slope for repeated disjoint unions
results.bound: B(mG) = m\Lambda(G) + O_G(1) where \Lambda(G) \ge F_k(G) is a computable rational from a finite optimization using at most k source words; the error is bounded independently of m and eventually periodic with computable period and threshold; B((m+h)G) = B(mG) + a for m \ge M with a = h\Lambda(G)
results.quote: For every fixed graph G with k=\chi(G), the number \Lambda(G) is rational and effectively computable. The maximum in (4.16) is attained by a distribution supported on at most k source words, meaning that at most k coordinates x_w are positive. Moreover, B(mG)=m\Lambda(G)+O_G(1), \Lambda(G)\ge F_k(G).

results.problem: Ordinary vs weak villainy difference under repetition
results.bound: B(mG) - B_w(mG) = m(\Lambda(G) - F_k(G)) + O_G(1); the difference is bounded if and only if \Lambda(G) = F_k(G), in which case it is eventually periodic; otherwise it tends to infinity linearly
results.quote: B(mG)-B_w(mG)=m(\Lambda(G)-F_k(G))+O_G(1). The difference is bounded if and only if \Lambda(G)=F_k(G). In that case it is eventually periodic; otherwise it tends to infinity linearly.

results.problem: Exact computation of villainy and weak villainy / threshold recognition
results.bound: Time h(B_w(G))(n+1)^c for exact computation of both B(G) and B_w(G) without either value supplied; f(t)(n+1)^c for truncated values min{B(G),t+1} and min{B_w(G),t+1}; fixed-parameter tractable in t with polynomial exponent independent of t
results.quote: There are computable functions f,h and an absolute constant c such that both B(G) and B_w(G) can be computed exactly on an n-vertex graph in time h(B_w(G))(n+1)^c, without either value being supplied. Moreover, given an integer t \ge 0, both min{B(G),t+1} and min{B_w(G),t+1} can be computed in time f(t)(n+1)^c for a computable function f.

results.bound: Unless P=NP, there is no fixed integer t for which recognition of B(G)=t is NP-complete; the same holds for B_w(G)=t
results.quote: Unless P=NP, there is no fixed integer t for which recognition of B(G)=t is NP-complete. The same conclusion holds for B_w(G)=t.
